app-store-reviews-scraper.note: cycle 833: only one real schema enum, `sort` (mostRecent/mostHelpful/favorable/critical). Unlike every other Actor in the facet-diff rotation, Apple's iTunes RSS review feed (itunes.apple.com/<cc>/rss/customerreviews/id=<id>/sortBy=<X>/page=<N>/json) is directly reachable from this box (no proxy needed, unlike google-news-scraper) -- probed sortBy directly with 13 candidate values incl. the 2 real ones plus 11 plausible-but-unlisted guesses (mostFavorable, mostCritical, topRated, newest, oldest, recent, helpful, rating, relevance, popular, trending). Only mostRecent/mostHelpful (the code's actual 2 API values) returned real entries (50 each); every other candidate returned HTTP 200 with an empty feed (no `entry` key at all) or HTTP 500 -- confirmed by inspecting the raw JSON body, not just entry count. favorable/critical are already correctly documented as client-side re-sorts of mostRecent, not real API params, so the 4-value schema enum is exhaustive and accurate. Clean audit, no code change. NOTE: cycle 832's queue note calling this 'the last enum_audit: null Actor' was wrong -- a fresh count after this cycle shows 12 Actors still null (ats-jobs, eu-ted-tenders, google-play-reviews, nih-reporter, remote-jobs, sam-gov-opportunities, sec-insider-trades, shopify-products, steam-reviews, substack, trademark-search, uk-find-a-tender). The rotation is not done; see queue.md. cycle 845: cycle 843/844 generalization applied here (watch baseline diffed against its own row shape). Apple keeps a review id stable when its author edits their own star rating (feed comment verified live 2026-09-26: a raw RSS entry has only author/rating/title/content/version/votes -- no developer-response field at all, unlike Google Play, so scoreChanged is the only applicable event here, not developerReplied/replyRemoved). Watch baseline was seenIds only -- no rating snapshot -- so an edited review was silently indistinguishable from an unedited one forever. Shipped watchEvents ([new, scoreChanged], empty = both) + watchEvent/previousScore output fields, backed by a seenMeta array (rating 1-5, 0 = pre-845 unknown, never fires) parallel to seenIds. Verified via 5 local round-trip scenarios against real live Apple review data (patching the LOCAL watch KV record, same technique as production KV patches in cycles 843/844, just local so nothing needed cleanup): (1) patched baseline rating differs from live rating + scoreChanged in watchEvents -> fires correctly with correct previousScore, exactly 1 of 20 pushed; (2) same patch + watchEvents:[new] (scoreChanged excluded) -> correctly silent, watchEventsFiltered counted, meta still updated to the live value so it cannot re-fire later; (3) meta silently re-synced after a fire -> third run byte-idempotent (0 pushed); (4) seenMeta key deleted entirely (pre-845 record simulation) -> zero false events, correct predates-change-detection log line; (5) a genuinely-absent id -> delivered as watchEvent:new, previousScore:null. Non-watch default-input regression byte-identical locally AND live on the platform (build 0.1.63, 5/5 charged). check-fail-ordering allowlist line numbers re-verified and updated (907/1146/1162, shifted from 815/1054/1070 by this change -- same 3 guard conditions read live in source, still safe). check-registry-fields/check-code-fields/check-readme-samples all clean after adding watchEvent/previousScore to registry.json output_fields + dataset_schema.json + README (input table, Watch mode section, Use cases bullet, new FAQ entry).

apple-podcasts-scraper.varied_test_note: cycle 893: FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BUG affecting a fleet-wide pattern, not just this Actor. input_schema.json podcasts field carried BOTH default and prefill = the Lex Fridman Podcast URL. Apify merges an input_schema default into ANY run (API/CLI/scheduler) that omits the field entirely -- so a buyer calling with only searchTerms set (the documented "find shows by keyword instead of ... giving URLs" path) silently ALSO got Lex Fridman Podcast episodes mixed into results with no warning, sharing the maxResults budget and starving the actual request (live-verified: searchTerms:["Darknet Diaries"], maxResults=6 returned 3 Lex Fridman rows + 3 real Darknet Diaries rows before the fix). Root cause: Apify distinguishes prefill (UI-only, never sent on omission) from default (merged into every run missing the field, including API calls) -- confirmed via Apify docs. Fix: removed the default key from podcasts in .actor/input_schema.json, kept prefill (Console one-click run UX unaffected). Live-verified post-push (build 0.1.48): searchTerms-only run now returns 6/6 genuine Darknet Diaries rows, 0 Lex Fridman; explicit podcasts input unchanged/still works; fully-empty input now fails cleanly via the Actor's own "provide at least one" validation instead of silently running Lex Fridman. Same default/prefill shape found and fixed in the SAME cycle on google-news-scraper (queries) and steam-reviews-scraper (apps) -- see their own varied_test notes. Not yet checked: app-store-reviews-scraper (apps/appNames) and google-play-reviews-scraper (appIds/searchTerms) have the same field shape and were NOT tested this cycle -- flagged in queue.md for the next QUALITY slot. | cycle 935: varied_test combo never exercised before -- watchLabel (episodes watch mode) crossed with MULTIPLE raw-RSS-only podcasts (no Apple id) in the same podcasts[] input. Found and FIXED a real cross-show identity collision: pushEpisodeRows() built watchId as `${row.collectionId ?? 'feed'}:${episodeId||episodeGuid||title}` -- every RSS-only show (collectionId always null for them, since scrapeEpisodesFromFeed passes null) fell back to the SAME literal string 'feed', not a per-show key, even though the adjacent floorKey/pairFloors logic already correctly disambiguates shows via `feed:${feedUrl}`. Reproduced live end-to-end with two synthetic local RSS feeds sharing an episode guid ("ep1", a realistic collision for cheap/DIY feed generators that guid by sequential per-show number): baseline over both feeds recorded only 1 seenIds entry instead of 2, and a later genuinely-new episode published on the second show (own distinct title/date, but happened to reuse guid "ep1") was silently reported as already-delivered -- 0 pushed, 0 charged, no warning, permanently invisible under that watch label. Fixed by falling back to the already-unique `floorKey` (not the literal 'feed') in the watchId formula -- zero behavior change for the Apple-ID path, where collectionId is always set and the fallback never triggers. Verified 3 ways + live: (1) local baseline with the fix now correctly records 2 distinct seenIds (`feed:<url1>:ep1`, `feed:<url2>:ep1`); (2) the same later-new-episode scenario is now correctly delivered (1 pushed) once its guid is genuinely its own; (3) Apple-ID watch regression byte-identical (5/5 seenIds unchanged, same `<collectionId>:<episodeId>` shape). Live on the platform (build 0.1.50): default-input gate SUCCEEDED 5/5 charged; a real single-feed raw-RSS watch baseline (feeds.simplecast.com) persisted seenIds as `feed:<feedUrl>:<guid>` in the shared production KV store, confirmed via the API, then the test record was deleted.

Live-verified post-fix: same locationKeyword="United States" query on lever+smartrecruiters -> 11/11 rows (9 lever + 2 smartrecruiters), all correctly showing country:"United States". Default-input regression clean (32/32 rows, all 7 ATS present, country values now consistently English: United States/United Kingdom/Netherlands). check-charges/check-pricing/check-code-fields all 0 drift. | cycle 927 varied_test: remoteOnly/isRemote pass across Greenhouse, Workday and default input. Found and FIXED a real bug in the Greenhouse mapper: `isRemote` was computed as `/remote/i.test(location) || (workplaceType ? /remote/i.test(workplaceType) : null)` -- `false || null` evaluates to `null` in JS, so any Greenhouse posting with no workplaceType metadata whose location text didn't literally say "remote" (confirmed live on stripe's board: "Dublin", "Chicago", "San Francisco, CA", "SF, NYC, SEA, CHI") came out isRemote:null instead of the correct false, even though the location text is exactly the evidence Workday's clean-boolean mapper uses to emit false for county names. Did NOT break the remoteOnly FILTER (!null is truthy, so those rows were already excluded correctly) -- purely a bad output value miscoded as unknown for any buyer doing their own true/false/null breakdown downstream. Fixed the fallback null->false (build 0.1.52), live-verified same stripe query goes from 9/10 null to 9/10 false (all real non-remote office locations) + 1/10 true unchanged (the one posting whose location literally says "Remote from the US"). Default-input regression clean (10/10 airbnb rows, same isRemote/workplaceType values as before). Checked the other 6 ATS mappers for the same `bool || (cond ? bool : null)` shape: Ashby/Recruitee/Workable/SmartRecruiters use native !!x booleans (never null-leaking), Workday uses a plain regex test (always boolean), Lever uses a ternary chain that only reaches null when every branch has genuinely run out of data (checked clean, not the same bug). Fleet-wide grep for the same `|| (... : null)` shape elsewhere found only string-building cases (apple-podcasts-scraper ID parsing, ats-jobs-scraper's own SmartRecruiters location string, grants-gov-scraper/substack-scraper text cleanup) -- none are boolean fields, so this was an isolated fix, not a fleet-wide pattern. check-pricing 0 drift/29, 3 services active, /health + /tools/ats-jobs-scraper both 200.

Pre-0.1.5 flat-string-id baselines decode to the no-snapshot marker and resync on first re-sight, so existing watches keep working and never fire against a backlog they never captured. Snapshot is only advanced on an actual delivery when PPE charging succeeds, so a charge cap defers a milestone instead of silently consuming it. Outputs `_watchChangeType`/`_watchPrevious`/`_watchMilestone`; `watchChangedCount` reported separately from `watchNewCount` in RUN_SUMMARY and the webhook.
